jobs.title: Director, Payroll Transformation
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 264681

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Director, Payroll Transformation leads the design, implementation, and modernization of enterprise payroll systems and processes across the organization. This role is accountable for delivering large-scale payroll transformation initiatives, with a focus on SAP HCM and/or SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll, ensuring system accuracy, operational continuity, and alignment across Human Resources, Technology, and Finance.

As a key leader within the transformation program, this role provides oversight and direction across all phases of payroll system delivery, including design, configuration, testing, deployment, and post-go-live stabilization. The Director will ensure payroll solutions are scalable, compliant, and aligned with enterprise standards, while supporting a seamless employee experience.

A core aspect of this role is to partner closely with cross-functional stakeholders to align business requirements with system capabilities, manage complex integrations across HRIS, finance, time, and third-party platforms, and ensure the successful execution of payroll transformation objectives.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will:

Lead end-to-end payroll transformation initiatives, including solution design, system configuration, testing, deployment, and stabilization activities.
Drive payroll testing and validation efforts, including user acceptance testing (UAT), parallel payroll runs, reconciliation, and issue resolution to ensure system accuracy and readiness.
Oversee system integration across HR, Finance, time, and third-party platforms to enable seamless data flow and end-to-end payroll processing.
Partner with HR, Technology, Finance, and external vendors to align system requirements, manage dependencies, and deliver transformation outcomes.
Ensure compliance with regulatory, audit, and governance requirements related to payroll processing, data integrity, and financial reporting.
Lead cross-functional workstreams and collaborate with program stakeholders to ensure delivery against timelines, scope, and quality expectations.
Support continuous improvement efforts by identifying opportunities to enhance payroll processes, systems, and overall operational efficiency.
Build and maintain strong relationships across stakeholders, fostering alignment, accountability, and effective communication throughout the transformation lifecycle.
Create an environment that promotes effective and efficient operations, ensuring alignment with Scotiabank’s Values and Code of Conduct, and supporting strong governance and control practices.

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed? We’d love to work with you if you have:

Post-secondary education in Human Resources, Business, Technology, or a related field; relevant SAP or payroll certifications are considered an asset.
Progressive experience in payroll transformation, HR technology implementation, or enterprise system delivery within complex, large-scale environments.
Strong understanding of SAP HCM Payroll and/or SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll, including system configuration, testing methodologies, and payroll operations.
Demonstrated experience supporting end-to-end payroll implementation, including design, UAT, parallel runs, and post-go-live stabilization.
Experience working across HR, Technology, Finance, and vendor partners, with the ability to translate business requirements into system functionality.
Strong project and program management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver within tight timelines.
Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and influencing skills, with the ability to engage senior leaders and cross-functional teams.
High attention to detail and a strong focus on accuracy, data integrity, and risk mitigation within payroll environments.
Ability to operate effectively within regulated environments, with familiarity in governance, compliance, and audit standards.
Strong leadership capability with a focus on collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Location(s): Canada : Ontario : Toronto

Scotiabank is a leading bank in the Americas. Guided by our purpose: "for every future", we help our customers, their families and their communities achieve success through a broad range of advice, products and services, including personal and commercial banking, wealth management and private banking, corporate and investment banking, and capital markets.

At Scotiabank, we value the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the Bank, and are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. If you require accommodation (including, but not limited to, an accessible interview site, alternate format documents, ASL Interpreter, or Assistive Technology) during the recruitment and selection process, please let our Recruitment team know. If you require technical assistance, please click here. Candidates must apply directly online to be considered for this role. We thank all applicants for their interest in a career at Scotiabank; however, only those candidates who are selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
About Inline

Inline is a Canadian mid-sized and growing civil engineering field services company of 550+ people, founded in 2012. We provide geomatics, materials testing, and geotechnical and environmental engineering to land development, infrastructure, oil and gas, industrial and mining clients, from nine branches across Western Canada and the North and operations in the United States. We have completed two acquisitions, most recently Challenger Geomatics in 2026, and are executing a five-year plan built on organic growth and further acquisitions. We have more than 90 employee shareholders and more than 20 Indigenous partners.

Inline has been named one of Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures and certified as a Great Place to Work.

Role Overview

Position Title: Chief Financial Officer
Department: Finance
Reports To: Chief Executive Officer
Direct Reports: Controller; Vice President, Finance and Integration
Works Closely With: Senior Leadership Team, Operations, People Operations, IT, the Board, lenders, auditors and partners
Location: Edmonton/Acheson, Alberta preferred; open to Calgary

The CFO leads Inline's finance function and is the CEO's partner on strategy, capital and acquisitions. The Controller runs the close and day-to-day reporting; the CFO oversees that work, sets direction, funds the plan and leads the finance side of growth. This is a hands-on role in a founder-led and operator-first company. You’ll work alongside operational leaders to give them reliable financial information, plan ahead for cash and capital needs, and lead the financial integration of new acquisitions.

Key Accountabilities

1.Strategy & Capital
Help the CEO and Senior Leadership Team decide where Inline plays and how it wins.
Partner with the CEO on the five-year plan, capital allocation and the balance between organic growth and acquisitions.
Lead budgeting, forecasting and long-range planning, and report results to the Senior Leadership Team and the Board.
Manage the mix, not just the total: margin by service line, sector and geography, and client concentration.

2.Treasury & Cash
Keep the business funded through seasonal swings and growth.
Manage cash flow and working capital through a highly seasonal business with a strong spring ramp-up.
Own lender relationships, credit facilities and equipment financing for a large fleet.
Manage deferred and vendor-financed acquisition payments.

3.Acquisitions & Integration
Make acquisitions a repeatable strength.
Lead financial due diligence, valuation, deal structure and closing, including working capital adjustments.
With the VP, Finance and Integration, fully integrate acquired companies: systems, processes, reporting and compensation.
Build a repeatable acquisition and integration playbook.

4.Field to Finance
Turn the work done in the field into accurate invoices, margin and cash.
Make sure field records, cost coding and invoices are right the first time, so billing and collections move fast.
Give business unit and project leaders margin data they can act on.
Lead the rollout of our new ERP across the group.

5.Oversight & Employee Ownership
Keep the numbers trusted and our employee-owners informed.
Oversee the close, reporting, audit and controls led by the Controller, across Canadian and U.S. entities.
Oversee accounting for our Indigenous partnerships and joint ventures.
Steward our employee share program: valuations, share transactions, liquidity planning and communication with employee-owners.

6.Finance Team
Build a finance team people want to join and stay on.
Lead and develop the Controller, the VP, Finance and Integration, and the finance team.
Bring finance into the field: help operations leaders understand and own their numbers.

What Success Looks Like in the First 12–18 Months

The ERP (Deltek / Vantage Point) goes live across the group on schedule and within budget, with Finance and Operations using it in their day-to-day work.
Challenger is fully integrated into Inline’s systems, processes, and reporting, and a documented integration playbook is ready for the next acquisition.
At least one new acquisition closes, with Finance leading the integration.
The time it takes to issue invoices and collect payment decreases measurably.
A rolling 13-week cash flow forecast and an annual capital plan help Inline anticipate and manage seasonal cash needs.
All entities complete a clean year-end audit.
The Finance team is stable and engaged, with clearly defined roles and responsibilities.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

CPA required; an MBA is an asset.
15+ years of progressive finance experience, including 5+ as a CFO or VP Finance.
Has bought and integrated several companies, from diligence through integration.
Experience in a project-based business such as engineering, construction or field services, including project accounting.
Experience in a multi-entity, multi-region, asset-heavy company of several hundred people.
Has successfully led an ERP implementation for a project-based business.
Experience with employee share ownership plans, Canada–U.S. cross-border financial operations, or accounting for Indigenous partnerships or joint ventures is an asset.

Skills

Strong commercial judgement: you understand how projects, crews and equipment turn into margin.
Credible with field leaders: you can explain margin to a site manager.
A builder, comfortable creating structure in a fast-growing company.
Hands-on: willing to do the work as well as lead it.

Our Core Values

Humble : Built from the ground up and have not forgotten where we came from.
Adaptable: There is always a way; you just need to find it.
Personable : Polite, courteous and straightforward.
Professional: Integrity, ethical and responsible for our actions.
Productive & Hardworking: We earn what we have.

Location & Compensation

Full-time, based in Edmonton/Acheson, Alberta (preferred) or Calgary, with regular travel to our branches and U.S. operations.
Base salary, a short-term incentive plan, a long-term incentive plan in stock options, and benefits.
The Chief Financial Officer position is fully on-site, with an in-person presence required to lead the Finance team and work closely with executive and operational leaders.

Director, Integrated Finance Services

Location:
Kingston, Ontario
Work arrangement:
Hybrid, minimum three days on-site per week
Workweek:
35 hours
Compensation:
$110,000- $127,000 plus Benefits

Altis Recruitment is partnering with a large, well-established post-secondary institution to recruit a Director, Integrated Finance Services
.
This opportunity comes at a significant stage of organizational transformation. You’ll help bring Finance teams together, strengthen financial advice across multiple faculties or shared-service portfolios, and establish a more consistent, collaborative approach to service delivery.
Reporting to the Executive Director, you’ll lead Finance Managers and build trusted relationships with senior academic and administrative leaders. We’re looking for an experienced Finance leader who combines sound financial judgment with an empathetic leadership style and the ability to guide people through change.

What you’ll do

Lead integrated Finance services across multiple portfolios, ensuring responsive, consistent and high-quality support.
Coach and develop Finance Managers, establish clear accountabilities and support effective decision-making within their teams.
Oversee annual and multi-year budgets, forecasts, financial models and reporting, identifying pressures, opportunities and sustainability risks.
Advise senior leaders on financial performance, resource allocation and strategic priorities, translating complex information into actionable recommendations.
Strengthen financial governance, internal controls, compliance and audit readiness.
Establish service standards, performance measures and escalation processes to improve accountability and client service.
Balance workloads and resources across teams, building resilience through cross-training, knowledge sharing and succession planning.
Lead recruitment, performance management and professional development while helping employees build a shared team identity.
Support process improvements, technology adoption and implementation of the new Finance service model.

What you bring

A university degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, Business Administration or a related field, and a CPA designation or equivalent recognized professional accounting qualification
.
At least seven years of progressive Finance experience
within a large, complex organization.
Significant experience leading Finance professionals through Managers, team leads or senior staff, including coaching, recruitment and performance management.
Broad expertise in budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling, reporting, internal controls and financial risk management.
Experience supporting multiple business units, departments or portfolios with competing priorities and diverse funding or revenue sources.
A track record of implementing organizational change, improving processes, introducing financial systems or transforming service delivery.
The ability to advise and influence senior leaders, communicate clearly with non-financial audiences and build consensus across stakeholder groups.
A collaborative, empathetic approach to leadership and the confidence to navigate sensitive relationships through change.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
Experience in higher education, healthcare, government, research or other complex, service-oriented organizations is an asset. Comparable private-sector experience is also welcome.

What’s offered

A leadership role with the opportunity to shape Finance service delivery across a complex institution.
A 35-hour workweek and hybrid working arrangement.
Pension participation and comprehensive health, dental and vision benefits.
Four weeks’ starting vacation, plus a paid holiday closure from December 25 through January 1.
Employee tuition assistance, family tuition support and childcare support, subject to eligibility and plan terms*
Potential relocation assistance, subject to approval.

Why Partner with Altis

If you’ve never worked with a staffing agency before, we make it easy. We work with top employers across Canada who have great jobs to fill, each vetted and verified by our team. When you apply for a job with Altis, we get to know you as a candidate and learn what your strengths are. Then, if you’re a solid match, we handle all the logistics, advocating for you as a candidate for the role, providing access to coaching and connecting you directly with the hiring manager. And rest assured, all our services are free of cost for candidates.

jobs.title: Director, Business Intelligence
jobs.description:
At Viral Nation,
we specialize in building social-first ecosystems for brands to connect with the modern consumer journey. Our integrated solutions align strategy, talent, media, and technology with culturally relevant creativity to scale the world’s fastest-growing digital brands. Viral Nation offers a fluid, creative, and growth-oriented environment that will support your ambitions to apply your talents in an open, collaborative, and fast-paced culture. Our ability to stay at the forefront of the industry has fuelled our success and will guide us in paving the path forward. We’re driven to push boundaries and think beyond today to deliver strategies, and we’re just getting started.

While we continuously exceed our goals, we need your help – our success is only as great as our people. Strong performance leads to high expectations, and we must keep raising the bar!

The Director, Business Intelligence will lead enterprise-wide analytics strategy and will be responsible for building and leading a high-performing team of analysts delivering actionable insights across sales forecasting, retail performance, campaign measurement, and influencer/paid/social strategy optimization.

This leader will serve as a strategic thought partner to Sales, Marketing, Brand, eCommerce, Finance, and Executive Leadership, translating data into commercial growth opportunities, driving ROI, and embedding analytics into core business decision-making. The role combines strategic vision, technical depth, cross-functional leadership, and team development.

Responsibilities:

Act as a senior analytics partner to client account, strategy, and service teams by translating client objectives into scalable, best-in-class measurement frameworks that support social-first marketing performance.
Serve as the senior analytics advisor to executive leadership, shaping marketing, retail, and social investment decisions through data-driven insights.
Elevate analytics from reporting to strategic advantage by synthesizing data into clear narratives that inform brand positioning, channel strategy, and enterprise decision-making.
Own end-to-end measurement strategy across paid media, influencer, social, and retail media, ensuring clear linkage between investment and revenue outcomes.
Forecast and quantify incremental revenue and retail lift across eCommerce and offline retail partners by developing predictive models that connect media spend, influencer engagement, and social performance to sales velocity and conversion.
Design and operationalize robust ROI frameworks, including brand lift studies, sales lift studies, incrementality testing, multi-touch attribution, and marketing mix modeling, translating insights into optimized channel mix and budget allocation.
Build scalable measurement systems to evaluate influencer effectiveness, content performance, audience growth, and conversion impact, informing creative strategy and platform optimization.
Identify emerging consumer and digital engagement trends to inform brand strategy, innovation, and go-to-market planning.
Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing analytics team, fostering a culture of analytical rigor, commercial acumen, and executive-ready storytelling.
Design and oversee scalable data collection and reporting infrastructure, including structured databases, automated reporting workflows, dashboards, and standardized presentations.

Qualifications:

Extensive experience in marketing, media, or agency environments, with demonstrated ability to apply analytics and research to drive client strategy and business outcomes.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a relevant field (Social Sciences, Statistics, Data Science, Business Analytics, or related discipline), or equivalent practical experience.
12+ years of progressive experience in research, analytics, and measurement, with a proven track record of leading complex, high-impact initiatives.
Advanced expertise in primary and secondary research methodologies, including brand tracking, brand and communications strategy, brand lift studies, regression analysis, Market Mix Modeling, social listening, and digital and site analytics.
Deep technical proficiency in analytics and BI technologies, including Python and SQL for analysis and data modeling, Google Cloud Platform, BigQuery, and Snowflake for data infrastructure, and BI tools such as Sigma or comparable platforms for scalable reporting and dashboarding.
Demonstrated ability to architect and optimize analytics workflows, data pipelines, and reporting systems that support automation, scalability, and self-serve insights.
Strong executive-level communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to translate complex analytical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Proven ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior client stakeholders, providing strategic guidance grounded in data, research rigor, and business context.

This role has an annual salary range of $140,000 - $160,000.

This range reflects the full scope and progression of the role, from building capability to operating with sustained impact at a higher level. In addition to base salary, we offer a comprehensive benefits and total rewards package designed to support our team as they grow with us.

Where an offer falls within this range is determined through the interview process. Candidates are benchmarked by the hiring team based on role scope, relevant experience, skill alignment, and expected impact, using consistent and objective criteria.

Compensation Philosophy:

At Viral Nation, compensation is structured, performance-led, and market-aligned. Pay decisions are intentional, based on role requirements, performance, and market alignment by country, and are set to maintain internal pay equity across comparable roles and levels.

Compensation progression is tied to demonstrated performance, expanded scope, and sustained contribution over time, not tenure alone. Employee compensation is reviewed regularly through formal performance reviews and check-ins to ensure alignment with role expectations and impact.

AI in Recruitment:

Viral Nation does not use AI-enabled tools to screen, assess, rank, or select candidates – our hiring teams make all hiring decisions. AI note-taking tools may be used during interviews.

DEI Commitment:

Viral Nation is committed to diversity, equity and inclusion in our agency. Viral Nation welcomes applications from people with visible and non-visible disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the recruiting and selection process.

jobs.title: Director of Product Strategy and Commercialization
jobs.description:
About TandemLaunch

TandemLaunch is a Canadian venture studio. Since 2010 we have created 30+ deep-tech ventures with a combined portfolio value exceeding $700M. We commercialize innovations in consumer electronics, hardware-enabled technologies, machine learning, and embedded systems, working directly with researchers from major university labs. We are one of very few venture studios globally with 15+ years of track record in building successful companies on research-backed deep tech.

About the Role

We are hiring a Director of Product Strategy and Commercialization to be the product-and-market voice inside several of our ventures at once.

These are companies with IP-backed technologies from cutting edge university research, a founding team, and on their first steps to commercial traction. Your job is to support our founders in identifying who would pay, get in front of them, carry the conversation through technical evaluation to a paid pilot or a design win, and feed what you learn back into what the venture builds next.

This is a leadership-track role that hinges on your ability to mentor and influence growing leaders. You will join our venture development team to help our ventures reach the necessary commercial traction to secure their next stage of financing.

What You'll Do

Own customer and partner engagements end-to-end
— from first conversation, through technical evaluation, to a paid pilot or design win. You find the buyer, you get the meeting, you carry it to money in collaboration with the venture’s leads.
Own product positioning and the customer-facing materials that support it
— product sheets, decks, demo strategies — across multiple ventures simultaneously.
Turn what customers tell you into product direction.
You are the person who helps the venture clarify the reasons to adjust their strategy in response to market needs, and collect the evidence that justifies it.
Run customer discovery and find the next market
— new applications and adjacent segments for ventures that are starting to get traction.
Represent ventures externally
at industry events, partner meetings, and customer conversations.
Mentor and directly work alongside our venture leads
as the commercial half of each venture team.

What We're Looking For

Requirements

5+ years of experience
in business development, product management, or strategy within a startup environment.
You have taken a technical product to a paying customer.
A purchase order, a paid pilot, a signed design win, a contract. Tell us what it was, who bought it, and what they paid. Grants, non-dilutive funding, maturation envelopes, accelerator awards and research scholarships are all valuable, but direct customer engagement is critical.
PhD/M.Sc/M.Eng degree or equivalent research-level technical fluency.
You can hold a real conversation with hardware engineers, ML researchers, or physicists — and are able to provide guidance on their technology strategy.
Professional French and English.

You have worked in ambiguity
— as a product lead, founding PM, co-founder, applications or solutions engineer, or the first commercial hire at an early-stage company.

Also true of the people who thrive at TandemLaunch

Genuine curiosity about novel technology.
You are comfortable navigating low-information environments to develop a strategy.
You are honest about what you do not know.

You might be coming from

Technical product management at a hardware or ML company · the first commercial hire at a deep-tech startup · applications or solutions engineering · product marketing for a technical product · technical sales or business development in B2B hardware · a founding team where you owned go-to-market.

What We Offer

A seat at one of very few venture studios globally with 15+ years of track record in deep tech.
Cross-portfolio exposure — ventures spanning AI, sensors, hardware, materials and audio in your first year.
Participation in fund economics through TandemLaunch's employee incentive pool — long-term upside that grows with the portfolio.
Direct mentorship from operators — co-founders, product leads and CEOs across the portfolio.
A supportive team that values curiosity, initiative and collaboration.

TandemLaunch is committed to building a community of excellence, equity, and diversity. We welcome applications from women, underrepresented minorities, persons with disabilities, 2SLGBTQ+ communities, and other candidates who will enrich our ideas and perspectives.

Industries

Venture Capital and Private Equity Principals

Challenger is fully integrated into Inline’s systems, processes, and reporting, and a documented integration playbook is ready for the next acquisition.
At least one new acquisition closes, with Finance leading the integration.
The time it takes to issue invoices and collect payment decreases measurably.
A rolling 13-week cash flow forecast and an annual capital plan help Inline anticipate and manage seasonal cash needs.
All entities complete a clean year-end audit.
The Finance team is stable and engaged, with clearly defined roles and responsibilities.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

CPA required; an MBA is an asset.
15+ years of progressive finance experience, including 5+ as a CFO or VP Finance.
Has bought and integrated several companies, from diligence through integration.
Experience in a project-based business such as engineering, construction or field services, including project accounting.
Experience in a multi-entity, multi-region, asset-heavy company of several hundred people.
Has successfully led an ERP implementation for a project-based business.
Experience with employee share ownership plans, Canada–U.S. cross-border financial operations, or accounting for Indigenous partnerships or joint ventures is an asset.

Skills

Strong commercial judgement: you understand how projects, crews and equipment turn into margin.
Credible with field leaders: you can explain margin to a site manager.
A builder, comfortable creating structure in a fast-growing company.
Hands-on: willing to do the work as well as lead it.

Our Core Values

Humble : Built from the ground up and have not forgotten where we came from.
Adaptable: There is always a way; you just need to find it.
Personable : Polite, courteous and straightforward.
Professional: Integrity, ethical and responsible for our actions.
Productive & Hardworking: We earn what we have.

Location & Compensation

Full-time, based in Edmonton/Acheson, Alberta (preferred) or Calgary, with regular travel to our branches and U.S. operations.
Base salary, a short-term incentive plan, a long-term incentive plan in stock options, and benefits.
The Chief Financial Officer position is fully on-site, with an in-person presence required to lead the Finance team and work closely with executive and operational leaders.

new_jobs.title: Director of Product Strategy and Commercialization
new_jobs.description:
About TandemLaunch

TandemLaunch is a Canadian venture studio. Since 2010 we have created 30+ deep-tech ventures with a combined portfolio value exceeding $700M. We commercialize innovations in consumer electronics, hardware-enabled technologies, machine learning, and embedded systems, working directly with researchers from major university labs. We are one of very few venture studios globally with 15+ years of track record in building successful companies on research-backed deep tech.

About the Role

We are hiring a Director of Product Strategy and Commercialization to be the product-and-market voice inside several of our ventures at once.

These are companies with IP-backed technologies from cutting edge university research, a founding team, and on their first steps to commercial traction. Your job is to support our founders in identifying who would pay, get in front of them, carry the conversation through technical evaluation to a paid pilot or a design win, and feed what you learn back into what the venture builds next.

This is a leadership-track role that hinges on your ability to mentor and influence growing leaders. You will join our venture development team to help our ventures reach the necessary commercial traction to secure their next stage of financing.

What You'll Do

Own customer and partner engagements end-to-end
— from first conversation, through technical evaluation, to a paid pilot or design win. You find the buyer, you get the meeting, you carry it to money in collaboration with the venture’s leads.
Own product positioning and the customer-facing materials that support it
— product sheets, decks, demo strategies — across multiple ventures simultaneously.
Turn what customers tell you into product direction.
You are the person who helps the venture clarify the reasons to adjust their strategy in response to market needs, and collect the evidence that justifies it.
Run customer discovery and find the next market
— new applications and adjacent segments for ventures that are starting to get traction.
Represent ventures externally
at industry events, partner meetings, and customer conversations.
Mentor and directly work alongside our venture leads
as the commercial half of each venture team.

What We're Looking For

Requirements

5+ years of experience
in business development, product management, or strategy within a startup environment.
You have taken a technical product to a paying customer.
A purchase order, a paid pilot, a signed design win, a contract. Tell us what it was, who bought it, and what they paid. Grants, non-dilutive funding, maturation envelopes, accelerator awards and research scholarships are all valuable, but direct customer engagement is critical.
PhD/M.Sc/M.Eng degree or equivalent research-level technical fluency.
You can hold a real conversation with hardware engineers, ML researchers, or physicists — and are able to provide guidance on their technology strategy.
Professional French and English.

You have worked in ambiguity
— as a product lead, founding PM, co-founder, applications or solutions engineer, or the first commercial hire at an early-stage company.

Also true of the people who thrive at TandemLaunch

Genuine curiosity about novel technology.
You are comfortable navigating low-information environments to develop a strategy.
You are honest about what you do not know.

You might be coming from

Technical product management at a hardware or ML company · the first commercial hire at a deep-tech startup · applications or solutions engineering · product marketing for a technical product · technical sales or business development in B2B hardware · a founding team where you owned go-to-market.

What We Offer

A seat at one of very few venture studios globally with 15+ years of track record in deep tech.
Cross-portfolio exposure — ventures spanning AI, sensors, hardware, materials and audio in your first year.
Participation in fund economics through TandemLaunch's employee incentive pool — long-term upside that grows with the portfolio.
Direct mentorship from operators — co-founders, product leads and CEOs across the portfolio.
A supportive team that values curiosity, initiative and collaboration.

TandemLaunch is committed to building a community of excellence, equity, and diversity. We welcome applications from women, underrepresented minorities, persons with disabilities, 2SLGBTQ+ communities, and other candidates who will enrich our ideas and perspectives.
